While looking at Calinou's gamepad testing review I noticed that the controllers' names are different on different platforms, and I found a related issue: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/96756 . I think this should be fixed in this PR, but I thought I might as well explicitly ask if that's something that should be fixed.
Should this PR also fix the mentioned issue and make the controllers have the same names on all platforms?

> I think this should be fixed in this PR, but I thought I might as well explicitly ask if that's something that should be fixed.
> Should this PR also fix the mentioned issue and make the controllers have the same names on all platforms?

There are good arguments for both. I would prefer keeping the names as they're reported by SDL3, and report this upstream if this hasn't been done already.

I've changed the code to work in a single thread just like older joypad implementations and removed the code for older implementations for Windows and Linux (MacOS code is shared with iOS so I can't remove it yet). The code should be ready for review again.
I've also made sure generic controllers (I have a cheap Sega Mega Drive-like controller from AliExpress) work with Windows and Linux (couldn't test MacOS for now but I'll try to do that too).

SDL supports selecting which subsystems to enable/disable:

https://github.com/libsdl-org/SDL/blob/1f6b5c681d788d3881a40c456bed5ce3e1a83aaa/CMakeLists.txt#L251-L275

But it seems they still compile (almost) everything anyway, and so there's some tight coupling in `SDL.c` or various cross-subsystem dependencies like `joystick` depending on `events`, which itself seems to include a `video` header...

@bruvzg and I will look into it further to see what could be done, or potentially discuss it with SDL maintainers to see if our use case of compiling only the joystick related APIs could be supported.

We can probably disable the SDL events subsystem so we can delete the other ones, and rewrite the code so it doesn't use SDL events.
For now it's not possible to disable all subsystems except the ones we use because SDL events uses them.

Going by skimming the code it seems that dynapi still isn't working? That definitely should be looked into, perhaps in a follow-up PR, as dynapi was introduced more or less exactly for the case of being able to replace statically linked SDL. It probably shouldn't be a showstopper for the initial merge, especially with Godot only using SDL for joystick input and not e.g. windowing, but even then getting dynapi working means end users being able to benefit from support for new controllers without having to update the game/engine.

Yes, we decided to make an exception to the feature freeze for this, as it fixes a lot of issues and maintainers are generally in favor of moving to SDL3. I think this actually warrants having the `bug` label too given how many issues it resolves.

I can't make promises as I still need to make a deeper review of the PR and we'll have to see how it fares under wider testing, but it should be able to make it in one of the next betas.

@dragonforge-dev If I understand correctly, you're looking for the SDL functionality I outlined in this proposal: https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/12407

I believe when this PR lands it would be fairly straightforward to expose that functionality from SDL in Godot.

I added a few commits (separate from now, we can squash later before merging) to improve the buildsystem changes somewhat:

- SConstruct: Add `sdl` option, `builtin_sdl` is meant for linking against shared
  libraries on Linux, not disabling the feature.
- SCsub: List files to compile explicitly instead of convoluted nested globbing.
- Linux: Fix support for linking against system SDL3 with `builtin_sdl=no`.
- macOS: Remove `use_lld` option, unrelated to this PR.
  * Feel free to open a new PR with that change, I didn't evaluate why it was needed.
- Windows: Fix C2099 compile error without disabling `/fp:strict`.
  * I'll propose that change to upstream SDL.
- SDL: Delete some more unused files.

I'm also adding a shell script to copy relevant files from a given SDL tag, so that it's not a manual and error prone process. This also simplifies how we document which files to copy since it's all in the script, and helped me find a few more files we could remove.

Finally, since SDL 3.2.16 was released, I updated to it.

With these changes, I'm pretty happy with the current state and I think we can merge it soon.

Some remaining questions (mostly for @bruvzg):

- Should we re-add Godot's own joypad code for desktop platforms as fallback if using `sdl=no`? It's not a lot of code so at least for 4.5, it might make sense to keep the option in case some users encounter any regression with the move to SDL.
- Can we go the extra length and implement support for Android, iOS/visionOS and Web now? It seems like it wouldn't be too much effort.
  * The current PR uses `SDL_PLATFORM_PRIVATE` with our custom definitions in `drivers/sdl/SDL_build_config_private.h`, which makes sense as we heavily customize which parts of SDL we build, so there's a number of defines we should set to 0 or not define. We can use https://github.com/libsdl-org/SDL/tree/main/include/build_config as reference for adding support for other platforms.
  * We might need to provide some hook for thirdparty platforms (e.g. consoles) to also provide their own `SDL_build_config_private.h`, in which case we could turn this to a define and have each platform set it in its `platform_config.h`. But there would likely be more that's needed, such as adding more SDL files to compile, so let's deal with that when the time comes.

> Some remaining questions (mostly for @bruvzg):

Discussed on Rocket.chat with bruvzg:

> * Should we re-add Godot's own joypad code for desktop platforms as fallback if using `sdl=no`? It's not a lot of code so at least for 4.5, it might make sense to keep the option in case some users encounter any regression with the move to SDL.

We don't foresee anything that our current code would be able to do that SDL couldn't, so let's go all in. We can always bring it back if we get regressions and need a quick workaround.

> * Can we go the extra length and implement support for Android, iOS/visionOS and Web now? It seems like it wouldn't be too much effort.

iOS/visionOS should be easy as it should be pretty much the same code we already have for macOS. Can be done as a follow-up (CC @stuartcarnie @bruvzg ).

For Android and Web we expect there's going to be a bit more work with Java and JavaScript code involved, so let's keep it for follow-ups (likely for 4.6).

---

So let's go ahead and merge. I'll squash the commits.
Once this PR is merged, I'll implement the iOS/visionOS version and remove all the redundant code.
